head_commit.message:
fix(build): remove hardcoded VS17 generator + /FORCE:MULTIPLE Linux leak (M2-N1)

Two independent build defects found from the latest Pipeline run
(34491277167, sha 9765888f):

1. Windows SDK cmake project() failure:
   CMakePresets.json hardcoded 'generator': 'Visual Studio 17 2022' on all
   5 Windows presets.  The win25-vs2026 hosted image ships VS2026 (v18), not
   VS2022, so the configure phase fails with 'could not find any instance of
   Visual Studio'.  Dropping the fixed generator lets CMake auto-detect the
   newest installed VS generator (same fix applied in round-4 22eea006d for
   individual workflow cmake -G calls, but the presets were missed).

2. /FORCE:MULTIPLE leaking to Linux linker:
   tests/unit/runtime-native/** CMakeLists called target_link_options(...
   PRIVATE /FORCE:MULTIPLE) unconditionally.  On Linux gcc treats the bare
   token as an input file path: '/usr/bin/ld: cannot find /FORCE:MULTIPLE'.
   Created a new chaos_native_force_multiple() helper that wraps the flag in
   if(MSVC), eliminating the leak.  18 call sites migrated.
   Also fixed t4_jit_call.asm: the MASM thunk was unconditionally set as a
   source file.  On Linux gcc treats .asm as a linker input (no object
   produced), causing 'cannot find ...t4_jit_call.asm.o'.  Guarded behind
   if(MSVC AND CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P EQUAL 8).

regression_check: cmake --preset windows-x64-reference configures locally.
Linux path logic verified via cmake -P script: chaos_native_force_multiple
is no-op on non-MSVC, T4 thunk empty.

head_commit.message:
wip(async): Task.Delay/GetAwaiter/IsCompleted native stubs — stop ChaosExternalRuntimeFallback→0

The await Task.Delay(n) path in async state machine dispatch ran:
  Task.Delay → ChaosExternalRuntimeFallback → 0 (null task)
  Task.GetAwaiter(task=null) → Fallback → 0 (null awaiter)
  TaskAwaiter.get_IsCompleted(awaiter=null) → Fallback → 0 (= false!)
  AwaitUnsafeOnCompleted(..., task_handle=0) → return 0 → NO continuation ever
  registered, state machine never resumed, Main never completed.

Fix:
1. ChaosAsyncTaskDelay: creates a real AsyncTask via async.h and immediately
   marks it finished via finish_async_task, so the caller gets a real task
   handle (not 0).
2. ChaosAsyncTaskGetAwaiter: returns the task handle itself (matching
   async_task_get_awaiter which does require_async_task + return task_handle).
3. ChaosAsyncTaskAwaiterGetIsCompleted: returns 1 (always completed), so the
   state machine runs synchronously on the resume path — avoiding thread-pool
   dependency while still exercising the full codegen dispatch.
4. ChaosAsyncTaskAwaiterGetResultValue: returns 0 (stub result payload).

All four registered as SimpleForward / DirectNativeSymbol in the
RegisterAsyncTaskYield helper alongside the existing YieldAwaitable bindings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(build): add missing include(cmake/chaos_native_test.cmake) in linux-arm64-smoke (M2-N1)

root_cause: the linux-arm64-smoke branch in CMakeLists.txt did not include
chaos_native_test.cmake, so macros like chaos_native_glob_add_tests were
undefined when tests/contracts/native/runtime-core/CMakeLists.txt tried to
call them at line 24.  The configure step failed with
'Unknown CMake command chaos_native_glob_add_tests'.

The windows-x64-reference and linux-x64-native branches both include this
file (added by round-7 and clang-tidy restoration respectively).

fix_strategy: add include(cmake/chaos_native_test.cmake) before the
add_subdirectory calls in the linux-arm64-smoke branch, same pattern as the
other branches that compile native test targets.

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): round-1 nightly fixes — restore + jit-baseline + hygiene (M2-N1)

Batch fixes from nightly diagnosis (run 34485489896):

1. gc-stress + native-integration: add missing dotnet restore + setup-dotnet
   steps before dotnet build --no-restore (NETSDK1004).

2. jit-baseline: add -DROADMAP0_PRESET_TARGET=linux-x64-reference to the
   Linux cmake configure call.  Without it CMake hits 'Unsupported
   ROADMAP0_PRESET_TARGET='' at line 875.

3. gc-perf: restore scripts/ci/collect-gc-metrics.py from acb5a2f2c.  The
   file was lost in the ci-r7-clean tree overwrite; gc-perf fails trying to
   import it from every workflow invocation.

4. hygiene: git-rm 8 scripts/debug/tmp_build_*.cmd files.  These are one-shot
   scratch files that should never have been committed; the hygiene gate
   flags them as a scripts-hygiene WARN that elevates to FAIL (WARN in CI
   mode triggers exit 1).  Also fixes release-governance WARNs (no v0.2.5
   tag + stale README mention) — these are advisory not blocker.

regression_check: all changes are CI-only or one-shot file removal; no
runtime/native code touched.  gc-stress/native-integration now have the
same restore pattern as codegen-unit and foundation-dll.

fix(build): provision googletest for linux-x64-native and linux-x64-reference (M2-N1/ENG-35138)

root_cause: foundation-dll smoke on Linux compiles tests/unit/runtime-native
gtest tests (gc_bit_utils, etc.), but neither linux-x64-native nor
linux-x64-reference branches in CMakeLists.txt provisioned googletest.  The
build died with 'fatal error: gtest/gtest.h: No such file or directory' at the
first gtest include in gc_bit_utils_test.cpp.

The windows-x64-reference branch had googletest (added when the CI round-7
gtest_main.lib fix was applied), and linux-arm64-native also had it (added for
the ARM64 JIT test harness), but the two x64 Linux branches were overlooked.

fix_strategy: add FetchContent googletest block (same URL_HASH as the Windows
branch, with gtest_force_shared_crt OFF for GCC) to both linux-x64-reference
and linux-x64-native branches, before fmt or any subdirectory that transitively
depends on gtest.

regression_check: same pattern as windows-x64-reference (line 77) and
linux-arm64-native (line 564) — confirmed working on those branches.
